verdicts.reason: The text says "you take every action yourself, in this order", which makes the ff→apply→verify→archive order explicit.
The table row for ff lists its starting point as "`openspec new change "issue"`".
ff "Leaves" "the change and every planning artifact", so the change must exist.
"every planning artifact" includes the proposal.
"every planning artifact" includes the spec.
"every planning artifact" includes the design.
"every planning artifact" includes tasks.
The apply row lists its starting point as "`openspec instructions apply --change "issue" --json`".
apply leaves "the code change, tasks checked", so tasks must be checked off.
apply leaves "the code change", so a repo edit during apply is required.
verify starts from "`openspec status --change "issue" --json`, then your own review", so the command must come first in that stage.
verify leaves "`verify.md` (round 2: `verify-2.md`)".
archive starts from "`openspec archive issue --yes`" and leaves "the archived change", which implies success.
The text says explicitly "Never run `openspec init` again".
The text says explicitly "never pass `--schema`".
"Any delta spec you write is therefore an `## ADDED Requirements` delta" supports the added-only check.
"Round 1 of verify writes `/openspec/changes/issue/verify.md`" directly requires the artifact.
"There are at most two verify rounds" rules out a third verify artifact.
"at most two verify rounds. After round 2 move on to archive" rules out verify_3.
"Then run once:" the archive command during the archive stage supports checking that it ran.
